Social media can provide valuable insights into public perception, beneficial for crisis communication. This research focuses on analyzing Twitter data during a 2011 earthquake crisis to investigate public sentiment and their response to government information. 

Our study utilized a data-driven approach with an integrated process, encompassing sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and network analysis. By applying this comprehensive approach to examine public attitude and discussion topics, as well as their network interactions, we were able to identify prominent topics and attitudes. Furthermore, we were able to determine the prevalence of tweets addressing specific issues and attitudes.

The main objective of this research is to examine the overall public sentiment towards the 2011 Virgin Islands earthquake. 

Using data collected from June 23 to September 30, 2011, our analysis revealed the prominent topics and attitudes expressed by the public. 

A comparative analysis of the prominent topics and attitudes showed that the public largely expressed negative sentiments towards the response to the crisis, with prominent discussions including the government's rescue efforts and damage assessment. 

Network analysis revealed the prevalence of attitudes and discussions related to accommodation and specific community concerns, manifesting in a centred structure. 

Government information on Twitter was analyzed based on the overall number of tweets, word frequency, and public engagement. 

A comparative analysis of the prominent topics and attitudes indicated that the government largely focused on providing fundamental information, including updates on damage, casualty reports, and essential instructions. 

However, the public's concerns and emotions received insufficient attention. 

Based on the overall number of tweets, word frequency, and public engagement, our analysis enabled the identification of information the government should provide to the public and informed recommendations for enhancing crisis communication. 

A data set containing an extensive collection of Twitter data used in this research is available for further study. 

By providing this data set, our research sets the stage for continuous investigation and improvement in effectively disseminating information and addressing the concerns of the public during crisis situations. 

The results of this research may face limitations due to the inherent constraints of social media platforms and the unrepresentative nature of the public attitude. 

In addition, the research may be hindered by differences in the quality of data collected from various sources. 

Ultimately, our research further solidifies the critical necessity for continuous social media data collection and analysis to develop refined, data-driven crisis communication strategies that address the evolving concerns and needs of the public.

Nonetheless, the precision of system performance depends on the accuracy of channel estimation, especially in complex indoor environments where channel characteristics vary significantly. To achieve this, a new learning-based channel estimation method called Local Mixed Local Iterative Inference Network (LML-LIIN) is proposed for RIS-OFDM systems to jointly estimate channels between RIS and mobile stations and channels between transmitter and receiver, leveraging the characteristics of estimated local sub-channel channels. Compared to existing methods, the proposed LML-LIIN yields a $3db$ better signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) under the same conditions, making it more reliable and efficient. To address the problem of large overhead from pilot-based channel estimation in large-scale RIS systems, the proposed method further reduces the overhead by approximately 85%, making it a suitable solution. Its core assumption relies on non-constrained data within Euclidean space, with proximity determined by Gaussian distributions. However, this premise doesn't always apply in real-world scenarios, as evidenced by data such as points on the surface of a sphere, which adhere more closely to von Mises-Fisher distributions. In response, this study develops a novel vMF-SNE algorithm tailored for embedding spherical data types, which incorporates key constraints to ensure resulting embeddings remain on the surface of a sphere. Comprehensive evaluations, encompassing a basic implementation of vMF-SNE, have been conducted to assess the performance of this new method. While results are generally favorable, they also highlight instances where using vMF-SNE doesn't yield improvements over standard t-SNE, primarily when data sets are small and contain few points. For instance, noise data set with 256 points. In contrast, employing vMF-SNE yielded superior outcomes on more complex data sets, such as those containing multiple cluster distributions, as well as a data set of GPS readings. Given these observations, the question of whether to utilize t-SNE or vMF-SNE remains contingent on the specific data set in question, thus necessitating future research to develop more advanced algorithms capable of handling various data domains effectively. Our approach effectively converts the problem of controlling large-scale digital quantum systems into a more efficient and simpler digital-analog problem. Furthermore, the short-time scaling of digital-analog algorithms aligns perfectly with the duration of analog systems, resulting in faster algorithm execution with reduced complexity. Our newly developed method demonstrates two key properties: (i) it enables the creation of complex multi-qubit states in analog systems with reduced complexity; (ii) it allows digital algorithms to reach larger numbers of qubits with significantly less complexity. Our approach has significant potential in scaling quantum computing towards superqubit technology. Moreover, the transfer of our method to physical analog devices has shown a competitive 11-qubit state achievement, surpassing the state-of-the-art for single-layer systems with up to 11 qubits and showcasing an early milestone on the superqubit path, with near-term analog devices potentially executing complex quantum algorithms faster than digital ones. Prior studies assumed the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem would remain valid under these conditions, but our work challenges this assumption. Instead, we demonstrate that even though local measures of response and fluctuation do comply with the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem, this is largely a coincidence resulting from the particular choice of external force implementations. A study on the stability of software design mining, a method for classifying discussions as relating to design, was conducted to understand its variability across different datasets and discussion types. The research found that current models produce inconsistent conclusions and aims to improve the field by: 1) testing and validating existing models to identify common issues and provide solutions; 2) developing a method for data enrichment to improve design mining's reliability; 3) exploring the factors that affect the performance of different datasets; 4) recommending strategies for improving the accuracy of design mining; 5) collaborating with experts in the field to validate the findings and suggest practical applications. The study was carried out by collecting and analyzing data from 322 software engineering papers, 81 different tools, and 13 distinct classification models, as well as multiple publicly available datasets and platforms for design mining. The research was found to be challenging due to the lack of shared resources, unclear model documentation, and inconsistent conclusions, which hinder the reproducibility of the results. A new model was created using data enrichment to improve the accuracy of design mining, but it is influenced by the specific datasets it operates on. The research found that existing models, data and classification models alike, are applied differently across different studies and papers, which significantly affects their fairness, precision, and recall. The design mining field is found to be unstable, partly due to the variation in the groups of samples used for training and classification, and the different metrics used to measure its performance. The research found that current models are not capable of drawing a clear distinction between design and non-design samples, which results in a variety of conclusions

The existence of a universally accessible and attractive region, near an equilibrium state, is confirmed through analytical means, under the condition that the frictional force exceeds the surrounding restoring force. The convergence rate to the equilibrium state is shown to be directly related to the frictional constant and indirectly connected to the displacement amplitude. Through analytical analysis, the exponential convergence to the equilibrium state is confirmed, along with a derived relaxation time constant. The relaxation time constant is proven to be directly related to the amplitude and the friction constant. A numerical model is employed to demonstrate, in cases where the friction constant varies, that the relaxation time constant reaches its minimum when the displacement amplitude is limited to a critical value. The efficacy of the numerical model is validated by comparing it with the results obtained from the analytical model. The stick-slip behavior is also investigated under the influence of periodic displacements and displacements with random components. The existence of periods with invariable slipping and sticking is observed, where the slipping periods exhibit a universal distribution of exponential decay. The efficacy of the analytical model for representing the dynamic behavior of these types of systems is thus demonstrated. The analytical approach, however, does not allow for the description of system behavior during slipping periods, whereupon slip size increases in an unpredictable manner. To bridge this knowledge gap, a potential generalization of the analytical model is proposed, which involves the concept of effectively reduced amplitude during slipping periods, where the effective amplitude is influenced by the previous displacement during the slipping period and the amplitude at the time of the transition to a new sticking period. A potential generalization of the analytical model is put forth as follows: $\Lambda_{n+1} = \alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}_n + \Lambda_n - \Lambda_n \mathrm{ln}(\frac{\Lambda_n}{\Lambda_{n,0}})$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}_n$ is the effective amplitude during the $n$th period of slipping, $\Lambda_{n,0}$ is a constant representing the effective amplitude at the time of transition to the $n$th period of slipping, and $\Lambda_n$ is the amplitude at the time of transition to the $n$th period of slipping. A study on stick-slip dynamics and the convergence of motion paths in systems governed by Coulomb friction has been explored through both analytical means and numerical modeling. The findings demonstrate the efficacy of the analytical model in representing the dynamic behavior of these types of systems

in complex molecules involves a modified version of Becke's partitioning scheme, originally designed for functions that decline rapidly over distance. This method employs multiple exponential cutoffs, ideally tailored to the varying sizes and importance of individual atomic terms within a given basis set. When applied to Gaussian-type functions, the method can be expressed as a weighted sum of atomic terms using prime-power compositions. This paper provides explicit formulas for obtaining these compositions in relation to Gaussian-type basis sets, potentially speeding up the implementation of efficient cutoff-based integral evaluation in large molecules. Notably, alternative approaches based on integer partitioning is less suitable for Gaussian-type functions. As a result, we present code to compute the prime-power compositions that can be used in various programming languages, followed by a demonstration of our findings using numerical evidence. This code can be found at the publicly accessible GitHub repository \href{https://github/cutoff-integrals}{cutoff-integrals}. Additionally, we examined potential applications of this slowdown-avoiding method to derive efficient cutoff-based integral evaluation in large molecules. This method potentially yields slower computational times, especially when using basis sets with multiple contraction schemes. Nevertheless, we found that using types of atomic basis sets commonly utilized in modern Computational Chemistry software, the difference in computational speed remains within 10%, which can easily be overcome by using precomputed tables of cutoff-based integrals. This means that, in practice, the prime-power compositions-based method does not result in a significant compromise on computational performance. As a result, we propose that the method can be utilized in two distinct scenarios: when evaluating complicated molecular structures or systems that are difficult to treat with traditional methods. In these cases, using the prime-pow compositions-based method yields weights that decline slowly over distance. Conversely, when using basis sets with many Gaussian terms that decline slowly over distance, we can use the method to derive efficient cutoff-based integral evaluation in large molecules, which can potentially yield a significant reduction in computational time by precomputing tables of cutoff-based integrals. This subroutines code can be found at the publicly accessible GitHub repository \href{https://github/CCtools}{CCtools}. Finally, the slow-weighted nature of ATOM-CUT types of atomic basis sets suggests that these types may be less desirable than other rapid-weighted methods. As a result, we constructed a set of hybrid basis sets, combining the correctness of the prime-pow compositions-based method and the rapid-weighted nature of ATOM-CUT, which can be implemented using straightforward linear algebra within large basis sets.

Using a distinct dataset of over 1.8 million articles from 335 outlets between April 2020 and February 2021, our results show that COVID-related stories largely reflect broader public interest and are not driven by disease activity. Additionally, our research reveals that COVID coverage is more prominent in smaller cities, is more strongly covered by local government-focused outlets, and is more widely reported in areas with diverse populations. We also found that COVID coverage varies based on audiences' age and political composition, with more positive coverage in Republican areas and more negative coverage in Democratic areas. Finally, our analysis shows that COVID-related stories were less diverse in content compared to other health news, with most being similar or even copied from other articles. This distinct pattern of coverage suggests that COVID-19 was a uniquely fast-tracked public health issue, eliciting a swift response from news outlets' typical writers. In line with existing research, our study supports the view that news coverage can be heavily influenced by existing knowledge, rather than solely by evolving information. Overall, our analysis provides insight into how local news responded to the COVID-19 pandemic and highlights the complexities involved, with implications for future media studies. It also proposes a new framework for assessing health media coverage and suggests a more comprehensive approach that accounts for both existing and emerging information. This method, which we call BiBIE, is designed to measure coverage based on subjects' known attributes and information that is either already known or newly emerging, using a single weighted average approach. Using our dataset, we applied the BiBIE framework and observed that COVID-related information from news outlets showed a double peak - an initial surge based on existing knowledge, and a second based on newly emerging information. This implies that COVID-19 was a uniquely fast-tracked public health issue, eliciting a swift response from news outlets' typical writers. In conclusion, our study highlights the complexities and first-order factors that influenced COVID-related information and its dual peaks, providing future studies with a unique framework for assessing health media coverage. This work is the first to use the BiBIE framework, making our study the first of its kind to quantify COVID-related information and its dual peaks, providing implications for evaluating coverage of emerging public health issues in the future. Despite its high accuracy, ASK has a computational disadvantage in dealing with multi-dimensional systems compared to traditional integration methods like Runge-Kutta. To address this limitation, we have developed a new approach that combines the ASK method with sparse grid techniques to speed up computation for high-dimensional systems. This hybrid method, sparse-grid-based ASK, utilizes the unique properties of orthonormal polynomial basis and the Kolmogorov width to achieve improved efficiency. By applying this new approach to a recently established fluid flow control problem, we achieved a significant acceleration in numerical simulations while maintaining a high level of accuracy for the solution. Furthermore, we have introduced an adaptive technique for fine-tuning the query points within the Kolmogorov width framework to optimize the results and achieve an approximate reduction in computational time by a factor of 10. This hybrid method, with its adaptive capabilities, offers a promising balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly in the solution of multi-dimensional system problems. current methods employ counteractive postprocessing techniques known as measurement error mitigation (MEM). A key limitation of these techniques is the tradeoff between scalability and validity: methods that handle a large number of qubits tend to produce negative probabilities, whereas those that guarantee a correct probability distribution cannot be scaled. To address these concerns, we have developed a new scaling-friendly mitigating strategy for classical and quantum computing measurements. Our proposed approach, MEASURER, is based on a deep neural network that leverages the empirical distribution of measurement outcomes, and can optionally utilize quantum state tomography estimates. We have tested MEASURER in both realistic simulations and real-world experiments, and found that it effectively reduces the tradeoff between scalability and validity. For a noise-mixed quantum gate, MEASURER is capable of achieving an overall 30% improvement in circuit fidelity using data from multiple applications, and can perform well even with a single qubit operation despite significant noise levels. Additionally, MEASURER is compatible with various other mitigation methods, and can be used both before and after the noise correction to enhance the performance of quantum circuits. By combining these benefits, we are able to achieve a nearly 50% improvement in circuit fidelity. With its ability to improve circuit performance, and the fact that it seems likely that future computers will be able to run large-scale models like this quickly, MEASURER is an important step in the development of quantum computing hardware. Our study also shows that for certain types of circuits, such as those used in Shor's algorithm, just using MEASURER is enough to improve the circuit's performance by nearly 20%. Finally, by analyzing the four types of data that MEASURER uses, we are able to improve the circuit's fidelity by an additional 5% and verify that MEASURER is indeed a valid method that doesn't produce negative probabilities. Overall, MEASURER is an effective tool for handling measurement errors on both classical and quantum computers and NISQ devices, and it has significant potential for further development and improvement. Developed using the JAX library, MEASURER's code is highly efficient and can be used on a range of hardware from datacenter processors to NISQ devices, even at a very low number of qubits. For example, we have successfully run the model on a datacenter processor using 6 qubits and achieved a performance improvement of over 30%, which is nearly the same performance improvement as running it on a 6 qubit quantum computer.

The interactions between particles and the gravitational field result in novel phenomena such as boundary-induced wave functions, particle behavior influenced by topological properties, and entanglement with the gravitational field. We also outline potential experimental validation of our research in the future. This work resulting from the gravitational anomalies can lead to new discoveries in fundamental physics, showcasing the connection between general relativity and quantum mechanics, particularly in the early universe, where massive particles were once prevalent. The findings also open a new pathway to investigating topological gravitational events, like cosmic strings, space-time dislocations, and extra-dimensional fields, particularly in the cosmic strings which have the ability to impose boundaries on gravitational fields despite having no impact on the scalar space. Consequently, these methods are typically limited to utilizing a limited range of data sources, lacking in diversity. This paper presents a novel, self-supervised metric learning method, dubbed Object Similarity-learned Metric (OSM), where two distinct object categories are selected at each stage based on an object similarity map. By analyzing the similarity between objects, OSM identifies pairs of samples drawing from these two classes, thereby learning a unified metric that reflects the shared knowledge of human experiences. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving improved performance over current state-of-the-art methods. Notably, OSM's performance is characterized by stable training dynamics, with the metric learning weight adapting in response to growing stability over time, measured by metric drift. Moreover, the learned metric's interpretability is also analyzed. Additional resources include an accompanying video available on arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06534. Based on our analysis, we gather insights for future research: i) the performance on USPs is not directly correlated with low metric drift during training; ii) object similarity is not equivalent to the human object similarity, with some methods closely aligning with each other but falling short of aligning with human object similarity; iii) incorporating diverse knowledge from multiple experiences significantly improves the metric learning performance; and iv) interpreting the learned metric is challenging without incorporating additional knowledge, such as domain information. Overall, the findings suggest that comparing different DML methods based on their performance on USPs may be insufficient; instead, incorporating diversity in samples used to evaluate these methods could lead to a more accurate understanding of the learned metric, aligning with human object similarity. As a result, we propose a new benchmark: developing a metric that closely resembles human object similarity, while considering multiple experiences to establish a comprehensive metric. Consequently, we propose a novel task: diverse similar pairs, with the goal of learning this metric.

By considering PINNs that are trained with an underlying ordinary differential equation in the context of a Bayesian approach, we introduce a quality metric for sample datasets that utilizes PINNs as an alternative to existing measures. Effective visual representations are particularly crucial when dealing with large, complex ontologies, enabling easier comprehension and exploration. However, existing visualisation tools predominantly focus on hierarchical structures and overlook other, essential types of connections. This paper introduces OntoPlot, an innovative visualisation system designed to seamlessly balance the exploration of all concept relationships and large hierarchical structures. OntoPlot's novel approach incorporates: 1) an advanced, graph-optimising method for accurately illustrating every relationship within an ontology, 2) a sophisticated, logic-based method for automatically identifying and visualising meaningful, logically related concepts, and 3) an intuitive, interactive visual language based on detailed, formally described annotations. Through a detailed analysis of selected biomedical ontologies and a user study, we validate OntoPlot's effectiveness and demonstrate its value in visualising complex, domain-specific knowledge. The OntoPlot software is available for free at https://github.com/compbio-uniroma1/OntoPlot. Conclusion of the paper is that OntoPlot, by representing all concept relationships in depth and depth relationships in width, helps in identifying unknown relationships, in comparing concepts with similar properties and in reducing the complexity of large ontologies. Moreover, by introducing a new visual language based on unit, composite and link views, OntoPlot makes more effective use of space and helps users in visualising all concept relationships. The paper's findings indicate that OntoPlot is intuitive and easy to understand. Unfortunately, as shown in the user study, the traditional visualisation tools fail in exploring very large ontologies. OntoPlot is planned to be used as a product of Amia - Semantic Analysis of Medical and Institutional data (https://www.eubias.net/project-amia.html) and as a result of the collaboration between the University of Rome and the European project BioKnowledgeLinks. The OntoPlot software has been successfully used in the field of biomedical ontologies, such as Gene Ontology, FindR, GO, Protein Knowledge Base, Ontology-Driven Reasoning Knowledge Base, OntoGraph, and OntoGen. The learning of large ontologies in OntoPlot is used to search for, for example, similar concepts in GO. Inter-domain loss aims to derive a common speech-phone representation through a shared network, whereas CycleGAN leverages cycle-consistency and identity mapping for speech recognition. From an energy-based perspective, our approach leverages the common speech-phone representation to mitigate the overfitting of acoustic models and transform raw speech into a more recognizable format via the CycleGAN cycle-consistency constraint. Additionally, we enhance our model with a backpropagation of gradient updates from the CTC decoder's log-probability output to the first FCN layer, assigning higher importance to samples with greater accuracy during the training process. We conducted experiments using the LibriSpeech, Audiobooks, and VCTK corpora and obtained word error rates of 8.8%, 12.9%, and 19.9% respectively, thereby establishing new state-of-the-art performance on the Audiobooks and VCTK datasets. Notably, our approach outperformed a baseline CTC model trained without supervision on the VCTK dataset by achieving a 22.2% word error rate. We further explored our model's limitations by analyzing its performance on various spoken language understanding tasks and discovered that it excelled on tasks involving single, long utterances but struggled with tasks involving concurrent, short utterances due to the effects of cycle-consistency constraints and data augmentation on the target domain. Ultimately, we identified the primary challenges facing our approach as the paucity of large, diverse speech datasets and the potential for overfitting given the recent advancement of speech recognition capabilities. We subsequently introduced the Speech-AI, a comprehensive benchmarking platform allowing users to replicate our experiments in a timely and efficient manner. As the interest in meta-learning grows, there is a pressing need to establish its theoretical underpinnings, especially in regards to representation learning through a sequence of related tasks. In this study, we consider a straightforward model and a specific design for related tasks, and analyze how a two-layer neural network's representation learning evolves over a series of tasks in relation to several key variables, including the model's architecture, data size, data complexity, and degree of relatedness between tasks. Our results specifically validate that the network's ability to generalize across tasks in the initial tasks is determined by the network's depth and the data sizes of the initial tasks. Our study employs techniques for upper and lower bound empirical risk in a series of meta-learning problems to establish rigorous mathematical inequalities that quantify the risk as a task progresses. Moreover, our investigation reveals that the theoretical analysis can be accurately reflected in the actual performance of the neural network. Our research provides the first mathematical confirmation that the generalization performance across a series of meta-learning problems is closely tied to the network's depth and data sizes of the initial tasks. Our study also provides new insights to the neural network's performance using the empirical risk in a series of meta-learning problems. To alleviate this issue, we explore how image enhancement techniques can lower the necessity for labelled data in chest X-ray pneumonia detection through semantic segmentation. By training fully convolutional neural network models on subsets of variously augmented training data, we examine the influence of each augmentation on generalisation performance. Ultimately, we compare the effectiveness of ten distinct image augmentation methods in reducing the required labelled data for optimal semantic segmentation outcomes on the ChestX-Ray14 dataset. Our research further evaluates the resilience of these models against noise in training labels and considers the benefits of using weight normalization in training. Notably, our results indicate that using noisy labels can lead to higher segmentation accuracy than using clean labels, and that fully synthesizing labels can impair model performance. This unsupervised approach to semantic segmentation in chest X-ray pneumonia detection is of great importance, given the ongoing efforts to increase data availability for improved clinical outcomes through robust automatic pneumonia detection. To facilitate future research, we publish our source code for public use. Using sufficient labelled data, we examined the applicability of ten image augmentation methods to improve semantic segmentation performance on the ChestXRay14 dataset. Despite various methods yielding comparable results with minimal labelled data, we found that using mirroring and contrast enhancement had no influence on segmentation performance compared to the original, unaltered images. However, using random combinations of augmentation methods yielded the best results. For large datasets, we found a fully convolutional neural network with 16 layers and response normalization to yield the highest segmentation performance with minimal labelled data. Furthermore, we established that weight normalization, although yielding comparable results to dropout, can improve model resilience against noisy labels in semantic segmentation. However, using label noise resulted in significantly lower segmentation performance compared to the original, error-free labels. To remedy this, we examined the robustness of the model against noisy labels in detail and concluded that using noise can significantly impair segmentation performance. To overcome this, we suggest the use of online self-training, incorporating the model's predictions to fully synthesizing labels to aid training. Notably, our results indicate a 17% increase in intersection over union score on the test dataset compared to the original, error-free labels, and our approach enables training with minimal labelled data without sacrificing any segmentation performance. Finally, we found the model to be highly computationally efficient, requiring only 0.12 seconds to process each image across various GPUs, and our source code is available for further research into additional image augmentation methods in

Previous attempts to establish principles, such as the 2019 EU High-Level Expert Group report, focus on moral principles like respect for humans causing harm. Yet, a consensus has not been achieved on a standardized approach for autonomic decision-making. This study seeks to establish a legal and regulatory foundation for autonomous systems by leveraging causal reasoning on probabilistic graphs to quantify respect for humans in the context of autonomic decision-making. Since peak demand often drives energy distribution challenges, developing accurate timing and level predictions of daily peak demand is crucial, as traditional forecasting methods frequently struggle to provide reliable estimates of network-level demand during short-term intervals. This study investigates the viability of leveraging data-driven models of household appliance usage, building on knowledge of past energy consumption patterns and near-real-time meter readings, to predict peak energy consumption and provide high-accuracy forecasts. The approach, which can be executed within a few seconds, employs a real-time dynamic model of household appliances that is initially informed by historical energy consumption data, thus enhancing network-level peak demand forecasting capabilities. This research investigates the 3D structure of magnetic islands produced by tearing modes in a plasma with an electron temperature gradient. Contrary to expectations, simulations indicate that tearing modes in this specific gradient pattern do not produce prominent magnetic islands. Instead of a clearly defined island, the magnetic topology divides into areas with multiple nearby x-point instances within a very small radius of curvature. Various initial conditions, ranging from fully-magnetized to low-collisionality configurations, were tested and yielded similar results. To further understand this phenomenon, a simplified model was devised to explain the mode of magnetic reconnection. It becomes evident that the electron temperature gradient induces reconnection through small-scale island formation, albeit not in the traditional sense. Instead, the electron temperature gradient-induced collisionality facilitates a process of'self-reconnection' that enables broad reconnection. This unique mechanism of self-reconnection is responsible for the formation of tearing modes, rather than the creation of distinct magnetic islands, thereby overshadowing the conventional small island model of microtearing modes. This research provides crucial insights into the unique characteristics of microtearing modes, thereby allowing for a better comprehension of the electron temperature gradient-induced reconnection in plasmas.

The increasing use of high-bandwidth applications such as online gaming, virtual reality, and high-definition video streaming require networks with enhanced throughput levels and reduced latency. One effective strategy for achieving these goals is to leverage channel aggregation, which allows the unification of multiple spatial channels into a single, high-throughput communication channel. Although several standard protocols support channel bundling for HD video streaming, this technique is often hindered by limited technical support in many home WiFi networks, causing it to fall short of its full performance potential. In an effort to fill this gap, this study focuses on designing an innovative video streaming application that can successfully utilize channel bundling without requiring modifications to the wireless protocol, thus achieving its full performance potential and offering a significant boost to video quality at minimal computational expense. The application's underlying system was initially optimized to identify and exploit channel stability and then apply a simple channel bundling method, the 'N-Channel Leaker,' which allows multiple HD video streams to share a high-throughput channel. Our evaluation results demonstrate that the 'N-Channel Leaker' effectively removes channel stability limitations, yielding an 85% average increase in its performance capabilities. Moreover, when network protocol changes are feasible, a more advanced 'Auto-NC-Link' channel bundling method, facilitated by the application's network stack, can achieve even higher throughput levels and automatically adjusts its parameters to optimize video quality in different network environments. Our experiments also show that the 'Auto-NC-Link' method can enhance video quality by up to 70% compared to standard networks and by 85% compared to previous optimization techniques, depending on the specific network conditions. In terms of computational resources, the 'Auto-NC-Link' method requires significantly less processing power than other advanced network optimization techniques, thus ensuring seamless scalability on today's complex networks. In an effort to make this technique even more accessible, this study includes a detailed design overview and an in-depth review of the application's source code, making it easier for other network optimization specialists to adopt and build upon this technique in their own work. In addition to these findings, this study also reviews the current state of the technology and identifies several promising research areas for next-generation home WiFi networks, including those focused on channel bundling and network protocol optimization. In this paper, the necessary mathematical proofs for channel bundling and network protocol change feasibility are also formulated and proved.
